units.source_text: “他写过一本卖不出去的有关胚胎学的书。

en.t: He had written a book on embryology that would not sell.

units.source_text: 在这本书的动植物名称的索引里，有诸如日本血吸虫、双壳贝、鸡、人。

en.t: In the index of plant and animal names in that book, there were entries such as Japanese blood fluke, bivalve, chicken, and human.

units.source_text: 你知道吗？

en.t: Do you know?

units.source_text: 在人的后面有个括号，内括‘见人类、人’。

en.t: After the entry for human there was a parenthesis saying, see mankind, human.

units.source_text: 人类也罢、草履虫也罢、天芥菜也罢，都是无区别的人类，反正它们都是藐视人类的。”

en.t: Mankind, paramecia, heliotrope, they are all mankind without distinction, and in any case they all despise mankind."

units.source_text: （他说过：注意鞋类倒是个不错的爱好，

en.t: (He had said, Paying attention to footwear is actually a rather good hobby,

units.source_text: 你不是曾在你父亲的医院里为女患者整理过鞋子吗，

en.t: did you not once arrange the shoes of female patients at your father's hospital,

units.source_text: 因此格外关注人家穿的鞋吧。

en.t: and that is why you pay special attention to the shoes people wear.

units.source_text: 再没有比受丈夫嘲笑更令人愤懑的事啦。

en.t: There is nothing more infuriating than being mocked by one's husband.

units.source_text: 简直就像是天芥菜的气味嘛。

en.t: It is just like the scent of heliotrope.

units.source_text: 是小姐廉价的香水味儿。

en.t: It was the young lady's cheap perfume.

units.source_text: 没错，刚才在正门门口看见小姐穿的草鞋，

en.t: Yes, the straw sandals I saw the young lady wearing just now at the main gate

units.source_text: 不是南部盛冈面儿的，确实是广岛面儿的。

en.t: were not made with Nanbu Morioka facing, but were certainly Hiroshima facing.

units.source_text: 我怎么竟把这点给忘了，而只顾关注她品味高雅的衣裳了呢？

en.t: How could I have forgotten that and noticed only her tasteful clothes?

units.source_text: 丝毫够不上讽刺嘛。）

en.t: It was not the least bit ironic.)

units.source_text: “我丈夫常说，没有比男人更幸福的雄性动物了。

en.t: "My husband often said that there is no male animal happier than a man.

units.source_text: 论形象和声音之优美，据说唯独人类的女性比男性优越。

en.t: In beauty of form and voice, he said, only human females are superior to males.

units.source_text: 诸如捕蝇蜘蛛、火鸡的雄性那样跳舞；

en.t: Some dance, like male jumping spiders and turkeys;

units.source_text: 金钟儿、金丝雀的雄性那样唱歌；

en.t: some sing, like male bell crickets and canaries;

units.source_text: 孔雀的雄性那样绚丽夺目的着装；

en.t: some dress in dazzling splendor, like male peacocks;

units.source_text: 麝香猫、灵猫的雄性散发香水般的芳香，

en.t: male musk cats and civets give off a perfume-like fragrance,

units.source_text: 大自然中献媚讨好的注定是男性，

en.t: and in nature it is the male who is destined to court and ingratiate himself,

units.source_text: 唯独人类的女性，集大自然中万般动物求爱方式之大成，向男性献媚讨好。

en.t: but human females alone gather together every method of courtship in nature and use them to charm men.

units.source_text: 据说苍天虐待雄性，是生物界的规律。

en.t: They say it is a law of the living world that heaven mistreats males.

units.source_text: 在生活里，动物中的雌性如此蔑视雄性，这也是为了孩子。

en.t: In life, when females among animals despise males in this way, it too is for the sake of the young.

units.source_text: 大自然保护母亲啊！

en.t: Nature protects the mother!

units.source_text: 丈夫揶揄我说：那么，女性同胞可以运用拒绝生孩子这种行为，

en.t: My husband teased me, saying, In that case, women can use the act of refusing to bear children

units.source_text: 对唯独把人类中的女性当作继子看待的自然界进行报复，

en.t: to take revenge on nature, which treats only human women like stepchildren,

units.source_text: 不就好了吗？！

en.t: and would that not be fine?!

units.source_text: 我回敬他说：世间最明确地知晓为子孙活着的是人类，

en.t: I answered him back: humans are the ones in this world who know most clearly that they live for their descendants,

units.source_text: 最清楚地知道不是为子孙活着的也是人类。

en.t: and humans are also the ones who know most clearly that they do not live for their descendants.

units.source_text: 既然知道这两点，肯定也会承受上天双方面的惩罚。

en.t: Since they know both of these things, they must also bear heaven's punishment from both sides.

units.source_text: 宗教和艺术，都是从人类不为子孙而活着这种思维中产生出来的。

en.t: Religion and art both arise from the idea that human beings do not live for their descendants.

units.source_text: 像你这样的，企图以人工制造孩子的想法，

en.t: An idea like yours, trying to produce children artificially,

units.source_text: 与对创世纪以前无生物世界的憧憬是同样的。

en.t: is the same as a longing for the lifeless world before Genesis.

units.source_text: 据说科学的道路是崎岖弯曲地通向死亡的冰河。

en.t: They say the road of science winds ruggedly toward the glacier of death.

units.source_text: 如同地球的运动活像个圆形那样，

en.t: Just as the motion of the earth seems almost circular,

units.source_text: 时间的流程也在描画着圆圈呢。”

en.t: the flow of time is also drawing circles."

units.source_text: 夫人记得自己曾冲着丈夫这样说过。

en.t: The lady remembered having said this to her husband.

units.source_text: 尽管夫人自己也明白，这些话都是毫无根据的胡说，

en.t: Although the lady herself understood that these words were all groundless nonsense,

units.source_text: 但是面对着夫人信口雌黄的这番乱语，

en.t: still, faced with this wild talk that the lady had uttered irresponsibly,

units.source_text: 小姐心中仿佛有一股郁积着叹息的自我恋慕。

en.t: there seemed to be in the young lady's heart a self-love heavy with pent-up sighs.

units.source_text: 实际上，小姐正处在被夫人凝眸观望着而不知所措的当儿，

en.t: In fact, the young lady was just then at a loss under the lady's fixed gaze,

units.source_text: 然而脸上绝不露出一丝笑容。

en.t: yet not the slightest smile appeared on her face.

units.source_text: 不知怎的，夫人觉得小姐这张脸越发美丽了，

en.t: For some reason, the lady felt that the young lady's face had grown still more beautiful,

units.source_text: 她不由得想起故乡教堂的牧师美丽的千金那番英语布道。

en.t: and she could not help recalling the English sermon once given by the beautiful daughter of the pastor at her hometown church.

units.source_text: 所以此刻小姐的沉默，夫人毫不介意。

en.t: So the lady did not mind the young lady's silence at all.

units.source_text: 而看见狗店老板站起身来的时候，

en.t: But when she saw the owner of the dog shop stand up,

units.source_text: 她感到震惊，宛如传教士遭受凌辱那样。

en.t: she was shocked, as though a missionary had suffered humiliation.
